Voltage Detection

This sample application demonstrates the LPC voltage detection function.

P2_2 detects the input voltage and triggers an LPC interrupt when the voltage is over the set threshold.

Note

  • The pins that can be used for voltage detection are P2_0 ~ P2_7, Vbat. Detection voltage threshold range: 80mV ~ 3200mV

Requirements

For requirements, please refer to the Requirements.

Wiring

Connect P2_2 to an external voltage input.

Configurations

  1. The following macro can be configured to modify the pin definitions.

    #define LPC_CAPTURE_CHANNEL             LPC_CHANNEL_ADC2
#define LPC_TEST_PIN                    P2_2

  2. The following macros can be configured to modify the trigger edge settings of the LPC comparator.

    #define LPC_VOLTAGE_DETECT_EDGE         LPC_Vin_Over_Vth        /*< Set this macro to select the LPC detect edge. Selectable parameters include LPC_Vin_Over_Vth and LPC_Vin_Below_Vth. */

Building and Downloading

For building and downloading, please refer to the Building and Downloading.

Experimental Verification

  1. When the EVB starts, observe the following log within the Debug Analyzer.

    Start lpc demo test!

  2. When P2_2 detects a voltage higher than 1000mV, it triggers an LPC_INT_LPCOMP interrupt. The Debug Analyzer logs an entry indicating that an interrupt has occurred as well as a log for the voltage detection interrupt.

    LPCOMP_Handler
LPC COMP

Code Overview

This section introduces the code and process description for initialization and corresponding function implementation in the sample.

Source Code Directory

The directory for project file and source code are as follows:

  • Project directory: sdk\samples\peripheral\lpc\voltage_detection\proj

  • Source code directory: sdk\samples\peripheral\lpc\voltage_detection\src

Initialization

The initialization flow for peripherals can refer to Initialization Flow in General Introduction.

  1. Call Pad_Config() and Pinmux_Config() to configure the PAD and PINMUX of the corresponding pins.

    void board_lpc_init(void)
{
    Pad_Config(LPC_TEST_PIN, PAD_SW_MODE, PAD_IS_PWRON, PAD_PULL_NONE, PAD_OUT_DISABLE, PAD_OUT_HIGH);
    Pinmux_Config(LPC_TEST_PIN, IDLE_MODE);
}

  2. Since LPC is located in the AON area, there is no need to call RCC_PeriphClockCmd().

  3. Initialize the LPC peripheral:

    1. Define the LPC_InitTypeDef type LPC_InitStruct, and call LPC_StructInit() to pre-fill LPC_InitStruct with default values.

    2. Modify the LPC_InitStruct parameters as needed. The LPC initialization parameter configuration is shown in the table below.

    3. Call LPC_Init() to initialize the LPC peripheral.

LPC Initialization Parameters

LPC Hardware Parameters

Setting in the LPC_InitStruct

LPC

Channel

LPC_InitTypeDef::LPC_Channel

LPC_CHANNEL_ADC2

Edge

LPC_InitTypeDef::LPC_Edge

LPC_Vin_Over_Vth

Threshold Voltage

LPC_InitTypeDef::LPC_Threshold

LPC_1000_mV

  1. Call LPC_INTConfig() to configure LPC compare interrupt LPC_INT_LPCOMP and NVIC. For NVIC-related configurations, refer to Interrupt Configuration.

  2. Call LPC_Cmd() to enable LPC comparison.

Functional Implementation

  1. When P2_2 detects a voltage higher than the set threshold of 1000 mV, it triggers the LPC_INT_LPCOMP interrupt. Within the interrupt function, print the relevant information and clear the interrupt flag.

    void LPCOMP_Handler(void)
{
    DBG_DIRECT("LPCOMP_Handler");

    //Add Application code here
    if (LPC_GetFlagStatus(LPC0, LPC_FLAG_LPCOMP) == SET)
    {
        LPC_INTConfig(LPC0, LPC_INT_LPCOMP, DISABLE);
        DBG_DIRECT("LPC COMP");
        LPC_ClearFlag(LPC0, LPC_FLAG_LPCOMP);

    }

    if (LPC_GetFlagStatus(LPC0, LPC_FLAG_LPCOMP_AON) == SET)
    {
        DBG_DIRECT("LPC AON");
    }

}
